meta.scene_summary: We are building infinite context models on top of a stack that is currently having an existential crisis.

cooking.headline: Let's Encrypt is shortening cert lifetimes, because manual labor is the best security feature.
cooking.summary: They are moving to 64-day lifetimes to force better automation and kill off manual certificate management. It is basically the digital equivalent of making you clean your room every two months so you don't live in a hoard of expired keys.
cooking.plain_english: Let's Encrypt is reducing the lifespan of its security certificates to 64 days to encourage systems to automatically renew them.

cooking.headline: LLM compression is getting so aggressive that models might soon fit on a grocery store receipt.
cooking.summary: Samsung researchers figured out how to shrink models to sub-1-bit, which is basically the AI equivalent of deleting your 'node_modules' folder to save space. We are officially reaching the point where your toaster will have more context window than your brain.
cooking.plain_english: Samsung researchers have developed a new method to significantly reduce the file size of large language models while maintaining their performance.

cooking.headline: Linux just learned how to squeeze more RAM into your RAM
cooking.summary: Linux is introducing a new compression method that treats your memory like a carry-on bag you're desperately trying to zip shut. It turns out the best way to get more speed is to just make your data smaller so it doesn't have to travel as far.
cooking.plain_english: A new Linux memory management technique compresses data stored in RAM to increase read speeds and overall system performance.

cooking.headline: A 1M-context model just dropped, because your AI needed more room for its baggage
cooking.summary: StepFun just released a massive context window model that can process enough tokens to read a small library in one go. It's perfect for when you need to dump your entire codebase into a prompt and pray the AI actually remembers the first line by the time it reaches the end.
cooking.plain_english: StepFun has released a new artificial intelligence model that can process up to one million tokens of information at once.

cooking.headline: Mozilla asked Microsoft to stop being annoying, Microsoft took notes
cooking.summary: Mozilla sat down with Microsoft to discuss their aggressive design patterns, which is like asking a landlord to stop charging for 'convenience fees' you never signed up for. It's a bold move, but we all know the browser wars are just a series of polite meetings before someone pushes a surprise update.
cooking.plain_english: Mozilla held a meeting with Microsoft to express concerns regarding the company's user interface and design choices.

cooked.headline: US government just revoked the 'Easy Mode' setting for hiring developers
cooked.summary: The US government is suspending a key green card program for major tech firms, effectively turning the hiring pipeline into a DMV waiting room. It turns out even multi-billion dollar companies aren't immune to the bureaucracy of a group project where the professor decides to change the rules mid-semester.
cooked.plain_english: The United States government has suspended a specialized visa program that allowed major technology companies to more easily sponsor foreign employees for permanent residency.

cooked.headline: OpenAI's revenue projections just hit a major merge conflict
cooked.summary: OpenAI's revenue is $20 billion lower than previously teased, which is a massive discrepancy for a company burning cash like a server rack in a sauna. It turns out that 'AI-scale growth' is just regular business growth, but with significantly more expensive electricity bills.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI's actual annual revenue is $20 billion lower than the figures previously suggested by the company.

cooked.headline: OpenAI retracted three math papers, proving even the smartest models can fail a pop quiz.
cooked.summary: The company pulled the research papers after discovering they didn't hold up, which is a bold move for a firm building the world's brain. It turns out that 'hallucinating' is a much less cute term when you call it 'academic research.'
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI has officially withdrawn three of its mathematical research papers due to accuracy concerns.

cooked.headline: SpaceX is currently speedrunning the 'leveraged buyout' phase of space exploration.
cooked.summary: SpaceX is borrowing so much cash for their Mars ambitions that creditors are starting to get nervous about the repayment plan. It turns out that gravity applies to your debt-to-equity ratio just as much as it does to a Falcon 9.
cooked.plain_english: SpaceX is facing higher financial risk because of the large amount of money the company has borrowed to fund its operations.

cooked.headline: Cutting down a rare forest to host cloud storage for cat memes
cooked.summary: We are bulldozing one of the last American chestnut groves to build a data center that will likely host nothing but redundant backups and low-res thumbnails. It turns out the most efficient way to save history is to destroy a piece of it.
cooked.plain_english: A rare chestnut forest is being cleared to provide land for a new data center facility.
